nodes.norm_label: the client does not guess entitlement — only 'no output columns' is a client-side disabled reason
nodes.rationale: FORBIDDEN (entitlement) and CONNECT (data-source unreachable) are only knowable from the server, so they surface as post-click errors rather than a pre-emptive disabled state. Inventing a client-side entitlement check would have been a lie about what the client actually knows.

nodes.label: Radix portal blind spot (the 'silent failure' was an observation error)
nodes.norm_label: radix portal blind spot (the 'silent failure' was an observation error)
nodes.rationale: An audit reported Run as dead (no network request, no console error, no toast) on a migrated worksheet. Every observation was correct and also exactly what a working modal parameter gate looks like: Radix renders the Run parameters dialog through a portal into <body>, but the audit's page reads were scoped to <main>, so the dialog was invisible to them. Any check reading <main> or using get_page_text (which defaults to article/main) will falsely report a working modal as dead; verification must screenshot or query [role=dialog].

nodes.label: Translated fallback by default via i18next instance, not a required parameter
nodes.norm_label: translated fallback by default via i18next instance, not a required parameter
nodes.rationale: The plan review asked for a required translated fallback parameter on getErrorMessage, which would mean editing 53 call sites. Resolving the default through the already-imported i18next instance gives the same no-English-leak guarantee in three lines instead of 53 edits, while still letting callers pass something more specific.
